transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-23
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (Galileo Head of ML Ops), Evan Ross (Galileo PM), Samir Patel (Galileo Data Eng)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, glad we could keep this on the calendar before the holidays, quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Nair: Priya here, Evan, Samir all good on our side.
[00:12] Evan Ross: yep, all present.
[00:15] Maya Chen: great. Diego is going to run through the quality results from the last run — we saw a bit of a regression after the model swap last week so want to surface findings and next steps.
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: ok thanks. quick context — we ran the 750 sample prompt set you provided + an extra 250 edge cases you flagged. Scored using your rubric: accuracy, hallucination, relevance. overall mean quality score dropped from 87 to 78 (on our internal 0-100 scale) after the variant bump. safety hit rate increased from ~1.2% to 3.7%.
[00:48] Samir Patel: can you clarify variant bump — is that the quantized checkpoint you rolled?
[00:53] Diego Alvarez: yeah so this was the v2-quant-light variant, it's faster but we observed slightly worse handling on rare medical abbreviations. some of the tokenization differences cause longer context drift.
[01:10] Dr. Priya Nair: that's worrying — our acceptance criteria for the pilot was pass rate > 90 and safety hits < 1%. we're now below that. what are the concrete failure modes?
[01:22] Diego Alvarez: two main buckets — 1) hallucination on less frequent entity types (rare drug names, site-specific codes), 2) actionable medical advice flagged by our / your safety rules (e.g., definitive prescriptions). examples in the deck: prompt 137 returns a recommendation phrased as "you should" instead of deferring.
[01:40] Evan Ross: are the safety hits false positives or true dangerous outputs?
[01:44] Diego Alvarez: a mix; about half are false positives where model used clinical phrasing that our guardrail flagged, the other half are borderline where the model crosses into prescriptive wording.
[01:58] Maya Chen: quick interjection — for context Redwood has a couple levers: 1) prompt templating and canonicalization, 2) guardrail rules in the Console (post-generation filters), 3) dynamic routing to a safer model variant for flagged prompts, and 4) token-level tuning like biasing. we typically combine approaches.
[02:18] Dr. Priya Nair: Priya — how intrusive is the guardrail? it can't block benign answers frequently or it will hurt UX.
[02:25] Diego Alvarez: agreed. we tuned thresholds for this run to be conservative which produced more false positives. we can loosen threshold and add a lightweight rewrite instead of drop — e.g., convert prescriptive text to advisory language.
[02:40] Evan Ross: what about prompt fixes? we've got a lot of upstream template variance across teams.
[02:45] Diego Alvarez: prompt canonicalization helped a lot in earlier pilots. we recommend: normalize entity formatting (e.g., drug names), include explicit role instruction ("you are an assistant that never provides prescriptions, only high-level guidance"), and add safety disclaimers in template. that alone improved pass rate ~5 points in tests.
[03:05] Samir Patel: ok, timeline question — if we supply 1k more labeled examples and a cleaned template set, how fast can you rerun?
[03:12] Diego Alvarez: with our Dedicated pilot infra, we can run a full 1k+ eval within 24 hours, but we need the examples in the format we asked for. Maya can share the eval spec again.
[03:22] Maya Chen: I'll send the spec after the call. also Diego, can you highlight the top 10 failing prompts for Priya's team?
[03:28] Diego Alvarez: yes — we'll attach the per-prompt failure notes and suggested template patch.
[03:34] Evan Ross: are there cost implications if we route flagged prompts to a safer (larger) model?
[03:38] Maya Chen: yes, routing to a higher-cost model for a subset adds unit cost only for those requests; we can estimate based on current traffic. For the pilot scale (low qps) cost is modest.
[03:47] Dr. Priya Nair: from compliance perspective we need audit logs for any routing and the content to be redacted in logs. does Redwood provide that?
[03:54] Diego Alvarez: yes — Console provides per-request tracing and audit logs. we can mask PII and integrate with your KMS for keys.
[04:02] Samir Patel: on data residency — we need EU-only logging for a subset of customers, is that supported in the pilot?
[04:08] Maya Chen: we support region pinning and private deployments; for pilot we can spin up EU routed endpoints in Dedicated — small infra lead time but doable.
[04:16] Evan Ross: any regression due to KV cache behavior? we noticed longer context sometimes.
[04:20] Diego Alvarez: good catch — the quantized variant had slightly different KV pruning heuristics which influenced longer sequences; we observed a few cases where earlier context dropped earlier than expected. patch is to adjust the cache window or fall back to non-quantized cache for long-context prompts.
[04:36] Dr. Priya Nair: ok. what about guardrail false positive reduction without making safety worse — any quick wins?
[04:42] Diego Alvarez: yes — run a lightweight classifier pre-check tuned to your label distribution (this is cheaper than always running the safety model). combined with a conservative post-generation rewrite reduces false positives by ~60% in our experiments.
[05:00] Evan Ross: from a scoring standpoint — can you share distribution rather than single mean?
[05:04] Diego Alvarez: yes attached CSV includes per-prompt scores, distribution, and waterfall charts. we highlighted 23 prompts with >10 point drop.
[05:12] Maya Chen: moving to next — pilot success criteria recap: Priya had pass rate >90, safety hits <1%, latency p95 < 600ms for 512 token requests. correct?
[05:22] Dr. Priya Nair: yes that matches. latency flexibility of +/-100ms is acceptable but quality is primary.
[05:28] Samir Patel: we also need SSO/SAML for the console and SOC2 material.
[05:33] Maya Chen: we'll include SOC2/ISO and SAML integration docs; I can send those after this call.
[05:40] Evan Ross: any blockers for running the next benchmark?
[05:43] Diego Alvarez: only the labeled examples and the cleaned template set. also a small config change to enable guardrail rewrite flow.
[05:50] Dr. Priya Nair: we'll prioritize getting those to you — Samir will own that.
[05:55] Samir Patel: yep I'll export the label file and send it by end of day 12/27.
[06:00] Diego Alvarez: great. technical note — for evaluation we recommend enabling per-token logprobs and tying thresholds to those; it helps distinguish confident hallucination vs low-confidence phrasing.
[06:12] Evan Ross: how noisy are the auto transcriptions in the report? a few names look off (eg, Redwood product names).
[06:16] Maya Chen: yeah the export sometimes munges product names, ignore that — we'll attach a corrected CSV and the example transcripts.
[06:23] Dr. Priya Nair: curious — what's the rollback plan if performance doesn't improve?
[06:27] Diego Alvarez: we can pin to the previous variant (v1-stable) while iterating on prompts/guardrails; routing rules let us fallback automatically on high-risk prompts.
[06:35] Evan Ross: pricing — can you share Dedicated tiers for 50k QPS? joking — but our pilot will be modest, like 10k tokens/day.
[06:43] Maya Chen: haha — yes we'll send pilot-specific pricing. for pilots we often recommend a small Dedicated pool + burst to Hosted if needed.
[06:50] Samir Patel: on the sample failures — will you include the exact tokens that triggered the safety classifier? we need to reproduce locally.
[06:56] Diego Alvarez: we'll include redacted token spans and the pre/post-generation payloads (redacted for PHI).
[07:06] Evan Ross: ok looks good. any legal/procurement asks we should be aware of?
[07:10] Maya Chen: they wanted SSO, SOC2, and an exportable audit trail — all standard. legal will follow after pricing.
[07:16] Dr. Priya Nair: timeline — we expect to make a go/no-go decision by mid January, earlier if the next benchmark looks good.
[07:22] Maya Chen: noted. Diego, recap the tech next steps?
[07:25] Diego Alvarez: rerun extended eval with guardrail rewrite enabled, include per-prompt failure notes, attach top 10 failing prompts, and test routing to v1-stable for long-context cases. target results by 2026-12-28.
[07:36] Samir Patel: I'll share labels by 2027-01-06 per earlier agreement.
[07:40] Maya Chen: I'll send pricing, SOC2 docs, and the eval spec today.
[07:44] Evan Ross: we'll look for those and schedule the decision meeting.
[07:48] Maya Chen: wrap-up — thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing with the artifacts. happy holidays!

Notes / artifacts referenced: per-prompt failure spreadsheet (link), scoring CSV (link), guardrail rules draft (link), Dedicated pricing deck (link).

End meeting.
